title: How to get your products recommended in ChatGPT Shopping
summary: Learn how to prepare your product catalog for ChatGPT Shopping with accurate product data, up-to-date offers, and clear, consistent product images.
body_text: Quick answer To get your products discovered in ChatGPT Shopping: Make every product easy to identify . Use specific titles and complete attributes such as product type, material, color, size, dimensions, and compatibility. Keep every variant accurate . The image, price, availability, product information, and landing page should all represent the exact version being shown. Use product images that make comparison easy. Show the product clearly, keep the item recognizable, and avoid backgrounds or compositions that obscure important product details. Maintain visual consistency across your catalog. Consistent framing, scale, backgrounds, and image quality make products easier to scan when they appear beside competing options. Photoroom helps sellers standardize product imagery across large catalogs, so new products and variants follow the same visual system without requiring manual editing one image at a time. Give shoppers enough visual information to evaluate the product. Use additional views or images when they help communicate shape, material, texture, fit, features, or other details that matter to the purchase. Keep prices, stock, shipping, and merchant information current. The product card should match what shoppers find when they continue to your store. Fix the catalog at the source. Improvements to product data and visuals should become part of your normal catalog workflow so the same accurate product record can support ChatGPT and other commerce channels. If you sell online, there's a good chance a shopper has already asked ChatGPT to find a product like yours. ChatGPT Shopping has turned conversational AI into a product discovery surface, less like a marketplace and more like a personal shopper who compares options and asks the right questions on the shopper's behalf. For e‑commerce sellers, this changes where the competition begins. Your product may be evaluated and compared before a shopper ever visits your store —and before your branding, your product descriptions, or your site design get a chance to make the case for you. Their first impression is now a product card built entirely from your product catalog data : image, title, price, reviews, features, availability, and merchant information. This does not create a secret new optimization discipline. ChatGPT still needs the same fundamentals that strong e‑commerce channels have always needed: a complete catalog, current prices and stock, clear attributes, trustworthy merchant information, and high-quality product visuals . What changes is how those elements are combined in a conversational, personalized buying journey. Photoroom helps sellers create clear, consistent product visuals across their catalog so products are easier to understand and compare when they appear alongside competing options. This guide explains how ChatGPT Shopping currently works, what sellers can control, and how to prepare the data and visuals behind every product card, without needing a large team or budget. What is ChatGPT Shopping? ChatGPT Shopping is not a separate marketplace that shoppers need to visit. ChatGPT Shopping is not a separate marketplace that shoppers need to visit. A shopper makes a request, and ChatGPT finds products that match their specifications. Depending on the query and product category, ChatGPT can show visual product results, compare options, ask follow-up questions, and link to merchants where shoppers can learn more or make a purchase. Because this all happens inside a conversation, shoppers can refine their search the way they'd refine a request to a knowledgeable friend: adding constraints like budget, size, material, or delivery timing, ruling out unsuitable options, and asking for alternatives as they go. What starts as "a black pair of pants" can turn into "a black pair of wool trousers, size medium, with free shipping, under $100." These searches are highly specific and high-intent, and traffic from them converts at twice the rate of traditional e‑commerce journeys . OpenAI's own research puts shopping-related queries at roughly 2% of all ChatGPT activity, or an estimated 50 million requests a day . For e‑commerce sellers, that means products are increasingly getting discovered and compared inside ChatGPT itself, not just on marketplaces or brand websites. That makes ChatGPT Shopping readiness a strong competitive advantage, and small businesses can start optimizing for it today. How does product discovery work inside ChatGPT? OpenAI hasn’t shared a public formula that explains why one product might appear for a search query and another might not. But they do describe the process at a high level: ChatGPT considers the shopper's request and context, then uses product information to identify relevant options. Unlike Google , ChatGPT doesn't rely on crawling alone. It also pulls from structured feeds that approved merchants push directly to OpenAI, along with publicly available product information, metadata, and retail sources like reviews When selecting a seller, ChatGPT may also consider factors such as availability, price, quality, and whether the merchant is the maker or primary seller. The exact mix can vary by product and shopping experience. Together, these sources make up what ChatGPT actually sees of your catalog. That includes your product images, which don't require a click-through the way they would on a traditional search result. A photo is part of the answer itself, shown alongside price, specs, and reviews. Here's a breakdown of the signals ChatGPT may draw on, why each one matters, and what you can actually do about it. What ChatGPT may use Why it matters What a seller can do about it The shopper's query and conversational context Defines the product, constraints, preferences, and trade-offs ChatGPT is trying to satisfy. Write product data that covers real attributes and use cases, not only broad category keywords. Merchant product data provided through ACP or other integrations Can give ChatGPT richer and more current catalog information. Can give ChatGPT richer and more current catalog information. Publicly available product information Helps ChatGPT research products beyond direct merchant feeds. Make product pages accessible, complete, canonical, and consistent with feed data. Other relevant retail sources Can provide reviews, merchant offers, or additional context used during comparison. Maintain consistent product identity and trustworthy information across channels. Merchant metadata Merchant metadata Merchant metadata This mix of factors makes consistency more important than optimizing any single input. A product title on your website, a price in your merchant feed, an image attached to a variant, and the availability shown at checkout should all describe the same offer. Contradictions—an outdated price, a listing shown as in stock when it's sold out, a photo that doesn't match the variant—can confuse both the AI agent pulling your products and the shopper trying to decide whether to trust the result. In other words: it's not just about getting your feed right once. It's about keeping an entire product catalog consistent as it scales across products, variants, and channels. That's a data problem and a visual problem, and for most small businesses, the visual side is the harder one to keep up alone. Photoroom covers the visual side of the product catalog—helping sellers turn raw product photos into consistent, professional listing images across an entire catalog in a fraction of the time it would take to edit them manually. How can e‑commerce sellers connect their product feeds to ChatGPT Shopping? OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) lets any merchant share product data directly with ChatGPT. For a small business, this usually means asking whoever manages your website or a developer to set it up. It's a technical project, but not one that requires a large team or a big budget to get started. A direct feed is useful because product catalogs change continuously. Prices, stock, delivery estimates, promotions, and variant availability can quickly become inaccurate. A structured, always-refreshed feed can help reduce the lag between your actual catalog and the product information ChatGPT receives. This integration isn't a substitute for a strong product page . ChatGPT's shopping research can use both merchant-provided data and publicly available information. The feed and the page should reinforce one another, rather than becoming two competing versions of the product. At a high level, here's what it takes to connect your product feed to ChatGPT: Apply : Submitting a feed is free and open to any merchant. Format your catalog : Organize your product information (titles, prices, stock, images, and shipping details) into the structure OpenAI expects. Send a starter version : Share an initial feed so OpenAI can confirm it's set up correctly. Keep it updated : Refresh your feed regularly so pricing, stock, and availability stay accurate as your catalog changes. For most small businesses, the technical setup is a one-time lift. The bigger, ongoing job is making sure the information in your feed, product catalog, and website stays accurate and complete. How Shopify merchants can participate in ChatGPT Shopping For Shopify merchants, product data is already integrated with ChatGPT via the Shopify Catalog. This allows you to skip the application process and the technical setup, but it doesn’t guarantee that ChatGPT Shopping will retrieve your products for relevant searches. E‑commerce sellers on Shopify who want to increase visibility in ChatGPT Shopping should start by optimizing their product catalog . Review whether every sellable product is active, whether variants are mapped correctly, whether images match those variants, and whether the product details are specific enough to support conversational requests. Photoroom's Shopify integration speeds up that process. Sellers can clean up and standardize images directly within their existing catalog, so improvements sync automatically rather than requiring a manual re-upload every time something changes. Why product images matter in ChatGPT Shopping ChatGPT's shopping experience is increasingly visual. OpenAI says shoppers can browse products visually, compare options side by side, and upload an image to find similar items. In that compressed comparison, the shopper needs to understand the product quickly: what it is, which variant is shown, what details matter, and whether the image looks trustworthy. Consider these two images: A studio-quality photo of a ceramic mug on a clean, neutral background, shot straight-on with consistent lighting and no distracting props. A photo of the same mug taken on a cluttered kitchen counter, at an angle, with shadows obscuring the handle and a price tag still attached. The first image lets a shopper register the product’s shape, color, and material in an instant—even if it's shown at a small size next to two or three competitors. The second forces the shopper to work for that same information, which is exactly the kind of friction ChatGPT Shopping is designed to remove. In a side-by-side comparison, the clearer image usually wins the shopper's attention first. Photoroom helps sellers create that visual consistency across the catalog without the manual work of editing individual items and images. E‑commerce sellers can remove or replace backgrounds , standardize framing, create additional product views, and process hundreds of assets at once . This is especially important for Shopify merchants, whose product data may already flow into ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog. A connected catalog distributes the assets it contains, including its inconsistencies. Shopify merchants can use Photoroom’s integration to unify and improve images without wasting time on manual uploads; any changes are automatically applied. How can e‑commerce sellers get their products discovered in ChatGPT Shopping? ChatGPT can only recommend what it can clearly understand. That starts with a product catalog that's specific, complete, and consistent across every field and image. Here's where to focus. 1. Upload your entire product catalog If a product is absent from your catalog (or unavailable to the relevant integration), ChatGPT can’t retrieve it from the source—even if it’s relevant. 2. Give each product a specific title Lead with the actual product type and the attributes that distinguish the variant. A title like 'women's waterproof hiking jacket, navy, size medium' supports more matching criteria than a brand-led slogan or creative product name. 3. Record specific and relevant attributes Record material, color, dimensions, capacity, compatibility, fit, condition, and other category-specific facts in the appropriate fields. 4. Write for conversational product constraints Shoppers rarely search ChatGPT using one or two keywords. Instead of asking for a suitcase, dress, or coffee maker, they describe a situation: a durable carry-on for a budget airline, a formal dress that works in hot weather, or a compact espresso machine for a small kitchen. Product data should cover the attributes that make those requests answerable. That doesn’t mean stuffing every imagined use case into the title. Keep core facts in structured fields, use the description to explain practical benefits, and add category-specific information that helps the shopper understand fit. 5. Make sure variants are accurate Each size, color, bundle, or configuration should have the correct availability, price, identifier, landing page, and image. A product card is only useful when it sends the shopper to the version of the product they actually selected. Images should align with variants, too: if a shopper asks for the sage green version of a linen throw pillow, ChatGPT shouldn't surface a product card showing the cream or terracotta version just because that was the only photo on file. Photoroom can help close that gap by generating consistent images across every color and size variant , so every version of a product has an accurate, high- quality image attached. 6. Keep prices, stock, shipping, and merchant information current OpenAI has identified availability and price as factors that can affect merchant ranking, along with shipping, returns, policies, and the maker’s identity. Outdated information can also lead to poor handoffs and undermine consumer trust. The product card should match what shoppers find when they continue to your store. 7. Highlight useful reviews and product evidence ChatGPT shopping experiences can compare reviews and key features. Valid, visible reviews, FAQs, detailed specifications, and clear supporting content help shoppers evaluate the recommendation after it appears. 8. Give shoppers enough visual information to evaluate the product Show the product clearly, keep the item recognizable, and avoid backgrounds or compositions that obscure important product details. Use additional views or images when they help communicate shape, material, texture, fit, features, or other details that matter to the purchase. 9. Maintain visual consistency across your catalog Consistent framing , scale , backgrounds , and image quality make products faster to scan when they appear beside competing options. For sellers managing growing catalogs, Photoroom makes that consistency achievable at scale : applying the same quality and standards across hundreds of images in a batch, rather than one listing at a time. How to audit your product catalog for ChatGPT Shopping ChatGPT doesn’t provide sellers with a complete organic-shopping performance dashboard. The steps below help you identify the strengths and weaknesses in your catalog and measure their improvement over time. Choose 10 to 20 priority products with strong margin, healthy stock, and complete catalog data. Write three to five conversational-style prompts for each product using relevant constraints such as category, use case, budget, material, size, delivery, or compatibility. Test both broad discovery prompts (e.g., "a cozy throw blanket for a couch, under $60") and prompts that closely match the product (e.g., "a chunky knit oatmeal-colored throw blanket, 50x60 inches, machine washable"). Record whether the product appears, which image and details are shown, the merchant and URL represented, nearby competitors, and any inaccurate information. Repeat the same prompt set on a fixed cadence. This audit is most helpful when you repeat it regularly and look for patterns: If products are continuously absent , inspect your catalog coverage and eligibility first If the products appear with incorrect details , that’s your signal to compare the feed, product page, and variant data. If products appear but are difficult to distinguish from competing products , revisit the product image, visible title, and overall presentation. Photoroom can help with that final layer by standardizing product images across the catalog, correcting inconsistent backgrounds or framing, and making sure each product and variant is represented clearly when it appears in visual comparisons. Shopify sellers can also use Photoroom’s Listing Score tool to evaluate search-preparedness across their entire catalog. Prepare your product catalog to appear in ChatGPT Shopping ChatGPT Shopping compresses much of the buying journey into a single conversation. A shopper can move from a vague need to a small comparison set without having to browse dozens of category pages. That creates an exciting opportunity for e‑commerce sellers—but only when your product catalog can clearly answer the shopper’s request. Small businesses can’t waste time optimizing every image for a new algorithm update or interface. But you can build a unified product catalog that remains useful across discovery systems: complete data, explicit attributes, accurate prices and stock, trustworthy merchant information, and images that represent every product consistently . This is the information ChatGPT agents need to surface relevant products, and that shoppers need to make a confident purchase. Photoroom helps e‑commerce sellers build product catalogs at scale , with accurate images , multiple product variants , and standardized framing across hundreds of products at once. Create studio-quality listing images , apply a consistent catalog standard, and make every product easier for shoppers to evaluate when ChatGPT places it beside the competition.
